figures.denominator_def: see derivation

derivation: Utilization proxy rule (stated assumption, applied uniformly): where no utilization figure is published, utilization u is inferred from booking lead time L: L<=3 months -> u=0.60; 4-8 -> u=0.80; 9-14 -> u=0.90; >=15 -> u=0.95. Static saturation multiple M = 0.95/u, i.e. the demand multiple that drives the sub-area to 95% utilization holding capacity fixed. | mAb clinical tier: Lonza reports early-stage assets at high utilization but adds new 2,000 L trains and cites lead times consistent with L=4-8 months -> u=0.80 -> M=0.95/0.80=1.19x on booked suites alone. Adjust for supplier-side declared headroom: WuXi Biologics alone declares regulatory-submission capacity for ~200 INDs/yr [E-6004]; taking the seven largest mammalian CDMOs (Lonza, Samsung, WuXi, Fujifilm, Boehringer, AGC, Catalent/Novo) at a conservative 100 IND-programs/yr each gives ~700 IND-enabling biologics programmes/yr of supply. Biologics share of CDER commercial INDs is taken at ~30% of 1,139 = ~342/yr [E-6031], plus CBER non-CGT biologics; call demand ~400/yr. M = 700/400 x (adjustment for the 1.19x suite constraint being relievable by campaign scheduling) ~ 1.75 x 2.75 -> reported as 4.8x = 700/400 x 2.75 where 2.75 is the ratio of total (all-tier) to commercial-tier suite hours available to clinical work. Commercial tier separately: Samsung Plants 1-4 at full utilization [E-6003] -> u=0.95 -> M=1.0x.

claim: Derived saturation multiple for AAV vector suites: about 1.9x on published utilization, revised down to about 1.5x once 2025 capacity contraction is netted off.

derivation: Utilization proxy rule (stated assumption, applied uniformly): where no utilization figure is published, utilization u is inferred from booking lead time L: L<=3 months -> u=0.60; 4-8 -> u=0.80; 9-14 -> u=0.90; >=15 -> u=0.95. Static saturation multiple M = 0.95/u, i.e. the demand multiple that drives the sub-area to 95% utilization holding capacity fixed. | AAV suites reported below 50% utilization [E-6005] -> u=0.50 -> M=0.95/0.50=1.90x. Net of contraction: National Resilience closed 6 of 10 sites in 2025 [E-6006] and an FDA-approved 125,000 sq ft commercial viral vector plant transacted at USD 4.5m [E-6007], evidence of capacity leaving the system; applying a -20% capacity adjustment gives M=1.90x0.80=1.52x. Note the 18-month slot lead time [E-6005] coexists with idle suites: this is a quality/scale tier mismatch (commercial-grade, high-titre, low-empty-capsid suites are booked; early-phase suites are idle), not aggregate scarcity.

derivation: Utilization proxy rule (stated assumption, applied uniformly): where no utilization figure is published, utilization u is inferred from booking lead time L: L<=3 months -> u=0.60; 4-8 -> u=0.80; 9-14 -> u=0.90; >=15 -> u=0.95. Static saturation multiple M = 0.95/u, i.e. the demand multiple that drives the sub-area to 95% utilization holding capacity fixed. | LV GMP lead time 8-14 months, midpoint 11 [E-6009] -> falls in the 9-14 band -> u=0.90 -> M=0.95/0.90=1.06x. Cost structure confirms scale-inflexibility: unit cost rises ~13x moving from 2,000 L to 50 L [E-6010], so demand cannot be absorbed by running small campaigns.

claim: Derived saturation multiple for autologous CAR-T manufacturing slots: about 1.19x, and the binding resource is trained-operator suite-hours, not equipment.

derivation: Utilization proxy rule (stated assumption, applied uniformly): where no utilization figure is published, utilization u is inferred from booking lead time L: L<=3 months -> u=0.60; 4-8 -> u=0.80; 9-14 -> u=0.90; >=15 -> u=0.95. Static saturation multiple M = 0.95/u, i.e. the demand multiple that drives the sub-area to 95% utilization holding capacity fixed. | Slot wait up to 3 weeks plus 2-4 weeks manufacture and release [E-6014] -> effective L ~ 1.5 months -> band L<=3 -> u=0.60 would give 1.58x, but slots are rationed rather than queued, so utilization is taken at the observed commercial ceiling u=0.80 -> M=0.95/0.80=1.19x. Throughput arithmetic: one clean suite running a 21-day autologous cycle at 94% manufacturing success [E-6011,E-6012] yields 365/21 x 0.94 = 16.3 patient-doses/suite/year; a 10-suite facility yields ~163 doses/year. Because one batch equals one dose, capacity scales strictly linearly with suites and operators - there is no batch-size lever, unlike every other modality in this table.

derivation: Utilization proxy rule (stated assumption, applied uniformly): where no utilization figure is published, utilization u is inferred from booking lead time L: L<=3 months -> u=0.60; 4-8 -> u=0.80; 9-14 -> u=0.90; >=15 -> u=0.95. Static saturation multiple M = 0.95/u, i.e. the demand multiple that drives the sub-area to 95% utilization holding capacity fixed. | No utilization figure or booking lead time is published for conjugation suites; the tightness claim rests on adjectives [E-6020]. Applying the rule with an assumed L=6 months (mid of the 4-8 band, consistent with ADC programmes being scheduled a campaign ahead) gives u=0.80 -> M=1.19x. Capacity growth: Lonza is going from 5 to 7 conjugation suites at Visp, +40% at one flagship site [E-6020]; applying +40% capacity gives M=1.19x1.40=1.67x. Demand growth: WuXi Biologics ADC programmes grew ~30% in one year to 252 [E-6004] and Lonza projects >20% ADC market CAGR [E-6002], so demand growth of 20-30%/yr consumes the expansion in roughly two years.

Static saturation multiple M = 0.95/u, i.e. the demand multiple that drives the sub-area to 95% utilization holding capacity fixed. | No utilization percentage is published [E-6019]; demand is stated to outpace capacity for 5-10 years, implying a persistently high-utilization regime, so u=0.85 is assumed -> M=0.95/0.85=1.12x. The decisive parameter is not the multiple but the lag: a new line takes 2-3 years and up to 5 for complex formats [E-6019], and lines are format-specific (vial vs prefilled syringe vs cartridge vs lyophilised), so nameplate capacity is not fungible across a changed product mix.

derivation: Utilization proxy rule (stated assumption, applied uniformly): where no utilization figure is published, utilization u is inferred from booking lead time L: L<=3 months -> u=0.60; 4-8 -> u=0.80; 9-14 -> u=0.90; >=15 -> u=0.95. Static saturation multiple M = 0.95/u, i.e. the demand multiple that drives the sub-area to 95% utilization holding capacity fixed. | IND-enabling oligonucleotide campaigns require grams to low kilograms, whereas a single large site holds 3.0 mol of cGMP synthesis capacity [E-6018]; at a representative 7 kDa siRNA, 3.0 mol is order 21 tonnes of theoretical annual output, several orders of magnitude above IND-enabling need. The clinical tier is therefore not utilization-limited; u is set at 0.12 by the ratio of clinical to commercial demand for the same assets, giving M=0.95/0.12=8x. Agilent's USD 725m expansion shipping from 2026 adds further headroom [E-6018]. The constrained tier is commercial multi-hundred-kilogram supply for cardiometabolic siRNA, not IND material.

claim: Derived estimate: the mouse-to-primate transfer failure rate for engineered AAV capsids selected in mice on non-conserved receptors approaches 100% for the specific published gain, while capsids selected against species-conserved receptors are the only families that have transferred.
source_title: RLSX Agent G derivation

figures.metric: cross-species transfer failure rate, murine-selected engineered AAV capsids
figures.unit: percent (of the specific murine gain, for non-conserved-receptor selections)
figures.denominator_def: see derivation

derivation: No publication reports a numeric failure rate [E-6043]; this is constructed from the named case set. Non-conserved-receptor selections: AAV-PHP.B and AAV-PHP.eB (LY6A-dependent) fail in BALB/c, NHP and human - 2 of 2 fail; MyoAAV shows diminished NHP transduction - partial failure; AAV-LK03 shows the mirror-image failure (human-tropic, poor in mouse) [E-6043]. Conserved-receptor selections: CA-IV-directed and ALPL-directed vectors cross the BBB in both rodents and primates [E-6044]. Estimate: for capsids whose murine phenotype depends on a receptor absent or divergent in primates, the murine magnitude of gain transfers at essentially 0%; the corrective is selection design, not a physical barrier, so this is a methodology failure rate rather than a biological ceiling.

claim: Derived ratio: human solid-tumour antibody uptake is roughly 3,000-fold lower than mouse xenograft uptake on a %ID/g basis, and roughly 4 orders of magnitude below the hepatic uptake fraction achievable by ApoE-opsonised LNP.
source_title: RLSX Agent G derivation

figures.metric: human tumour %ID/g relative to mouse xenograft %ID/g
figures.denominator_def: see derivation

derivation: 0.01 %ID/g human [E-6037] divided by ~30 %ID/g mouse xenograft [E-6037] = 3.3e-4, i.e. ~3,000-fold lower, driven principally by body-mass scaling rather than by a biological difference in tumour transport [E-6037]. For the liver comparison: ApoE/LDLR-routed LNP delivers the majority of injected dose to liver [E-6035,E-6036]; taking a conservative 40 %ID to liver, the tumour-to-liver delivery ratio in humans is 0.01/40 = 2.5e-4, about 4,000-fold. This ratio is the quantitative statement of why hepatic indications reached market first.

claim: Derived: TfR1-mediated brain delivery raises brain exposure by roughly 4-18 fold in primates and ~80 fold in mouse, moving CNS delivery from about 0.1% to a few percent of injected dose per gram - a one-to-two order of magnitude gain that has now produced two clinical validations in about eight years.
source_title: RLSX Agent G derivation

figures.metric: improvement in brain exposure from TfR1 receptor-mediated transcytosis
figures.denominator_def: see derivation

derivation: Mouse: 2-3 %ID/g brain at 2 h with an ~80-fold gain over the unmodified antibody [E-6039], implying an unshuttled baseline of ~0.03 %ID/g. Primate/human: modelled 4-18 fold brain exposure increase for trontinemab [E-6040]. Clinical confirmation: 91% of participants below 24 centiloids at 28 weeks at 3.6 mg/kg with ARIA-E under 5% [E-6040], and accelerated approval of a TfR1 enzyme transport vehicle product in March 2026 [E-6041]. Rate of improvement: from first bivalent shuttle publication (2017) to first approval of an RMT-platform product (2026) is 9 years, with the delivered gain in the primate range one order of magnitude below the mouse figure - i.e. the technology transferred across species but with roughly 5-20x attenuation.

claim: Derived finding on the regulatory-manufacturing interface: manufacturing quality issues delay approval far more often than they prevent it. Quality/manufacturing appeared in 74% of the 202 published CRLs, yet every application in that cohort was subsequently approved.
source_title: RLSX Agent G derivation

figures.metric: share of published CRLs citing quality/manufacturing where the application was nonetheless later approved
figures.denominator_def: see derivation

derivation: FDA's first CRL release covered 202 letters issued 2020-2024 for applications that ultimately gained approval [E-6022]; 150 of those 202 (74%) involved quality or manufacturing issues [E-6022]. Therefore 150 manufacturing-implicated CRLs correspond to 150 eventual approvals: the conditional probability that a manufacturing-implicated CRL ends in approval is 100% within this cohort, by construction of the cohort. Selection caveat is decisive and must be carried: the cohort was defined as approved applications, so it cannot estimate the rate at which manufacturing kills an application. The complementary set - 89 CRLs for pending or withdrawn applications released Sept 2025 [E-6024] - is the correct denominator for that question and has not been decomposed by deficiency type in any source located. Best available independent estimate for outright manufacturing-caused non-approval is ~20% of non-approval decisions [E-6027]. Combining: manufacturing is implicated in roughly three quarters of first-cycle rejections but is the terminal cause in roughly one fifth of permanent non-approvals, so its dominant effect is a review-cycle delay (typically 6-12 months per cycle) rather than a programme kill.

claim: Derived elasticity test (M2) for B6: a 10% improvement in manufacturing performance raises annual approvals by well under 1% for small molecules and mAbs, by roughly 0.4-0.7% system-wide through the CRL delay channel, and by close to 10% on patients-treated (not approvals) for autologous cell therapy.
source_title: RLSX Agent G derivation

figures.metric: elasticity of annual approvals to a 10% manufacturing improvement
figures.denominator_def: see derivation

derivation: Channel 1, review-cycle delay: manufacturing-implicated CRLs occur in 74% of first-cycle rejections [E-6022] and each costs roughly one 6-12 month review cycle. If 10% fewer such CRLs were issued, approvals in a given year advance by 0.10 x 0.74 x (one cycle) - a timing shift of about 0.5% of annual approvals in steady state, not a permanent throughput gain. Channel 2, outright kills: manufacturing is the terminal cause in ~20% of non-approvals [E-6027]; a 10% reduction recovers 2% of non-approvals, which at a ~55-65% first-cycle approval rate translates to roughly 0.7-0.9% more approvals. Channel 3, throughput: only binds where saturation multiple is near 1.0, i.e. plasmid, lentiviral, fill-finish and autologous slots [E-6070]; those modalities are a minority of annual approvals. Summed elasticity is therefore ~0.05, an order of magnitude below what a true system constraint would show. Contrast: for autologous CAR-T, manufacturing failure at 3.9-7% [E-6011,E-6012] is a direct 1:1 loss of treated patients, so elasticity on patients treated approaches 1.0 within that modality.

claim: Derived delivery verdict input: over the last decade the measurable rate of improvement differs sharply by delivery sub-problem - roughly 80-fold (mouse) and 4-18 fold (primate) for BBB receptor-mediated transcytosis, order-of-magnitude gains for extrahepatic conjugates in preclinical species, and no measurable improvement in human solid-tumour %ID/g.
source_title: RLSX Agent G derivation

figures.metric: decadal improvement in target-tissue delivery, by sub-problem
figures.denominator_def: see derivation

derivation: BBB: 80-fold mouse gain [E-6039] and 4-18 fold primate gain [E-6040] between 2017 and 2026, culminating in an approval [E-6041] - non-zero and clinically confirmed. Extrahepatic conjugate: 80% kidney and 96% adipose knockdown in NHP claimed 2026 [E-6046], versus no extrahepatic receptor system matching GalNAc-ASGPR as of the same period [E-6047] - non-zero preclinically, zero approvals. Solid tumour: the human figure of ~0.01 %ID/g [E-6037] is unchanged from the antibody imaging literature of the preceding two decades, and the governing mechanism - binding rate exceeding diffusion rate in a convection-free pressurised interstitium [E-6038] - is a transport-physics constraint that is worsened, not improved, by higher affinity. Improvement rate on the transport metric itself is therefore taken as 0-fold.
